observations: My 30000-document adversarial tilde corpus still shows the 4 `misread` rows of round 1, the same documents (adv-1327, adv-14547, adv-17797, adv-23052), with regressions 0 and churn 0. Main refused those writes; the head stores them. Their tilde reading matches the engine. What still differs is an autolink literal (www after `!`, email after a letter or `|`) or an inline HTML node inside a strike, which Go stores with no strike mark. Main stores the same differences for text with no tildes.

Go's email autolink takes `~` into the local part, so a strike next to an email reads differently: `a~b~x@y.co` is one link to `a~b~x@y.co` in Go, while the engine strikes `b` and links `x@y.co`. Also `~~a c~~x@y.co`: in Go the link takes the closing `~~`. The cause is goldmark's linkify, present at the fork point too. dispatch://INFRA-531's plan replaces linkify with micromark's transform, which covers it; I reported the shapes to the architect.
